issues.description:
Method return type mismatch for Stock.take(String):
- problem_statement.md (UML) declares Stock.take(String): int (line 51).
- template repository implements public boolean take(String ingredient) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java (line 43), returning true/false.
- solution repository implements public int take(String ingredient) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java (line 43) and SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() in src/de/tum/cit/ase/SealSaloon.java (line 28) expects an int return code (-1 on missing/out-of-stock).
This inconsistency between the template and the problem/specification/solution will confuse students and can cause compilation errors or incorrect logic when they implement SealSaloon.checkOrderReady() or other code that expects integer status semantics (e.g., -1 for failure and a non-negative remaining quantity on success).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template's Stock.take signature and behavior match the UML and the solution: change the method signature in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java from 'public boolean take(String ingredient)' to 'public int take(String ingredient)'. Implement it to return -1 when the ingredient is missing or out of stock, otherwise decrement quantity and return the new quantity (as in the solution). Update any Javadoc/comments in the template to document the -1 failure code and adjust any template callers/tests accordingly so the API is consistent across problem statement, template, and solution.
